The language instead asks which attainable result can change the decision and whether it is worth its full burden. A sufficient answer is useful even when a broader ambition remains unresolved.

## STR.Preface:3 - Forces - What the comparison must hold together


Several tensions shape strategic work. Current obligations compete with development; flexibility has carrying costs; multiple feasible futures can favour different choices; and affected people may bear consequences that the decision holder does not experience. Evidence can arrive too late to help. Advice can be useful without granting authority.

Keep these differences visible. One numerical score cannot by itself settle conflicting values, an unmet protected condition or an unavailable permission. A local improvement can also consume the very shared resource that makes the whole strategy feasible.

## STR.Preface:4 - Solution - Connect the results the question needs


The four Parts group related problems for finding and reading. They offer a reading order; actual work follows the questions and available results described below.

Part I helps locate the strategic concern and uncertainty. STR.1 identifies the subject, decision and scope; STR.2 relates a material change to its actual premise; STR.3 frames the uncertainty and problem; STR.4 constructs futures that discriminate among choices. A changed source can finish at STR.2 without a new scenario exercise.

Part II develops directions, possible obtaining ways and their support. STR.5 finds or qualifies a worthwhile contribution and makes a sufficiently developed direction usable as a conditional filter. STR.6 recovers or constructs explained whole options, develops reusable material and retains useful possibilities. Its material-development entry can precede a settled receiving contribution; its coupled entry examines ways against changed problems. FPF C.39 supplies the unknown-way explanation Method, and C.40 supplies material development with its conditional coupled problem-and-solution entry. They are contributions to these live questions, not compulsory preliminary stages. STR.7 selects and designs only worthwhile bounded experiments; STR.8 connects the promised contribution to capabilities, dependencies, business models and initiatives. Existing evidence can make another experiment unnecessary.

Part III connects comparison to a responsible choice. STR.9 compares robustness, nonlinear exposure and option value, using a qualified PSD.12 response test only when needed; STR.10 examines actual commitments and affected-System consequences; STR.11 separates retained alternatives, intended joint use, advice and authorized commitments. A comparison does not allocate work, and a small authorization need not settle the larger direction.

Part IV supports revisiting and sustaining strategic practice. STR.12 turns qualified signals into bounded follow-up; STR.13 compares and maintains the strategy practitioner's Methods; STR.14 reconciles simultaneous work across horizons and scopes; STR.15 addresses actual cultural continuation and deliberate influence. Enter these directly when that is the problem, rather than repeating Parts I–III.

Results connect by the content needed for the next question. A lead about a new recipient may first need a qualified problem/contribution account before STR.5 can form a direction. A direction can then support STR.6's search for whole obtaining ways. Available material and a known operation can instead support direct development in STR.6 before the contribution is settled. Where problems and ways change together, the target result determines the next problem or way question. If the contribution or way is already sufficient, start from that result. If search exposes a different receiving problem, return that question rather than forcing it into the old option family. These are conditional uses, not a compulsory sequence.

An adequate PSD uncertainty or robustness result can likewise be reused without repeating its analysis. A missing data permission blocks the dependent use, not every option. A material joint-capacity conflict can reopen a commitment while leaving its framing and independent evidence intact.

**Constituent actions in ongoing work.** During strategy work, interpreting one changed operating assumption can constitute part of evaluating an option, while that evaluation is part of forming a commitment. A changed resource horizon alters which interpretation and option remain usable. People may understand the strategic ambition and perform the component calculations yet lack the intermediate Method for constructing a realizable option. STR.6 and STR.8 address the obtaining way and capability connections; they do not supply missing capability merely by describing it. FPF B.1.5.EW helps recover this vertical. Work already devoted to exploring an option does not establish that its later realization is available.

## STR.Preface:5 - Recognition and assurance - Understand the move, then support the claim


Ordinary descriptions let a reader recognize a direction, option, trial or cultural practice. Recognition alone does not establish feasibility, actual performance, authority, evidence strength or cultural persistence.

Use the direct source and professional guidance for the claim that matters. Keep observed conditions, estimates, hypotheses, recommendations, plans, decisions and performed work distinct. Stronger claims need their own support; missing stronger evidence need not erase a smaller independently supported result.

## STR.Preface:6 - Archetypal grounding - Three unlike applications


[SensorCo](#strapplication1---app-str-01---choose-sensorcos-response-to-commoditized-ai-inspection) follows one strategic question through the language. Its four-day preparation competes with a viable device improvement; the twelve-month direction remains open. The first-month ninety-versus-eighty-day conflict concerns the whole proposed arrangement, including those four days. A reduced seventy-eight-day proposal preserves reserve and a separately costed fallback but does not establish capability or authorize its whole scope.

[The professional-practice case](#strapplication2---app-str-02---a-professional-considering-a-new-practice) tests personal choice, livelihood and eight available hours against a twelve-hour proposal. STR.5's personal example begins earlier, before the contribution has been selected; STR.6's diagnostic example follows a search for an unknown obtaining way and stops at its evidence gap. Its separate synthetic-record extension develops material for a selected contribution, explores it before a contribution is chosen, and tests a transfer under changed conditions. [The public-service case](#strapplication3---app-str-03---a-public-service-under-deep-uncertainty) tests a protected access condition that a favourable average cannot cancel. These constructed cases show use and limits, not empirical effectiveness.

## STR.Preface:7 - Bias-Annotation - Whose contribution and whose burden?


Corporate language can privilege commercial return, executive authority and measurable effects. A personal or public-service use may have different purposes and decision holders. Preserve those differences instead of copying SensorCo's criterion.

Available evidence and visible participants can hide an affected group, tacit work or unpriced burden. Recover what can change the decision, including a competent objection, without turning every strategic question into unlimited discovery.

## STR.Preface:8 - Conformance Checklist - Correct use of the connected language


- The strategic subject, receiving question, horizon and holder of the actual choice are clear.
- An unsettled problem, a direction, an explained obtaining way and an examined exploratory intermediate remain different results; a sufficient result permits direct entry.
- A serious feasible rival, including continuation or stop, is not omitted to favour novelty.
- Evidence and comparisons concern the same options, configuration and conditions.
- Further inquiry has an attainable decision contribution worth its full burden.
- Whole commitments preserve material constraints, affected interests and displaced work.
- A retained alternative, joint-use selection, recommendation and authorization stay distinct.
- Capability, permission and financing claims come from their actual qualified contributors.
- Reconsideration reaches the affected decision in time; independent useful work is preserved.
- Method-worth and cultural-continuation claims retain their separate basis.

These questions connect the pattern-specific answers. Reuse a qualified local result when the combination does not change its conditions; inspect the whole configuration when shared constraints can invalidate otherwise adequate parts.

## STR.Preface:9 - Common Anti-Patterns and How to Avoid Them


**Strategy as a forecast deck.** A single expected future replaces comparison. Use discriminating futures only where their differences change the choice.

**Experiment by default.** More activity is treated as learning. Compare the attainable answer, whole burden and a sufficient decision on current evidence.

**Direction as permission.** A fitting initiative borrows authority from an adopted slogan or filter. Obtain the actual bounded commitment and its independent conditions.

**Success by component.** Several affordable initiatives overuse one team. Compare their simultaneous whole and the work they displace.

**Culture by publication.** A template or archive is treated as ordinary enactment. Ask what people actually transmit, recognize, select and retain.

## STR.Preface:10 - Consequences - What changes in practice?


Participants can stop with a useful bounded answer, preserve meaningful alternatives and commit only what the present basis supports. A qualified negative result can save work; a small preparation can keep a larger choice open; and a timely signal can change one commitment without discarding independent results.

The language requires comparison effort, source qualification and attention to shared conditions. It does not remove uncertainty or guarantee a superior outcome. Some questions remain blocked by unavailable evidence, capability or authority, and a worthwhile current course can coexist with that limit.

## STR.Preface:11 - Architectural Rationale - Why a connected repertoire?


One linear strategic-planning cycle would simplify teaching but would force unnecessary stages on direct questions and hide simultaneous work. Fifteen independent checklists would improve retrieval but lose the dependence among contribution, capability, whole cost and commitment. The selected repertoire keeps direct entry and the explicit relations needed for a connected answer.

FPF supplies common reasoning about evidence, choice, alternatives, configuration-relative contribution, practice architecture and culture. Those Methods do not alone explain the domain connection among strategic direction, business model, capability and cross-horizon commitments. Strategy supplies that connection while leaving actual advising, professional comparison and realization with their direct owners.

Several developing subjects can matter together: the external offering, organization, person and enabling platform. Changing one can require another contribution without making them one object or assigning one owner to all development. Small internally sustained improvement remains a serious alternative to a new large project.

Search and choice also differ. Finding a worthwhile contribution can finish with a provisional problem and a discriminating question. Finding an obtaining way can finish with an explained candidate and one missing condition. Those results support different next actions, so a separate search stage is not imposed on every use. Retaining a stepping stone can improve later possibilities without making it the best current commitment. A direction's filter can change which proposals qualify, but a revised rule does not rewrite earlier observations or allocate resources. These distinctions explain why direction, option formation, comparison, commitment and later reconsideration remain independently useful contributions.

The same reasoning preserves a separate method and culture question. A method can be worthwhile but unused; an archive can be available without transmitting a practice. Neither an annual method refresh nor a universal culture programme follows from using this framework.

## STR.Preface:12 - SoTA-Echoing - Current contributions, bounded transfers


The language combines source contributions because they change these working choices, not because their labels form a complete theory of strategy. Current scenario and deep-uncertainty methods inform discriminating futures, robustness and timely adaptation. Dynamic-capability and entrepreneurial-judgement work keeps agility, affordable loss and capability commitments conditional. Experimentation and set-based design research informs worthwhile inquiry and selective retention.

The language distinguishes discovery of worthwhile results from construction of obtaining Methods, preserving method plurality, useful intermediate possibilities and reasoning that later work can reuse. It also connects continuous organization development, different developing subjects and revisable comparison grounds. The [source-use account](#strreference1---source-use-and-currentness) explains the framework's synthesis alongside external contributions, serious alternatives and their limits.

These sources support particular Methods and choices, not an empirical claim that the whole language improves every organization. Historical anchors remain history where a later contribution is the current line for the question. Reopen a source-dependent choice when new evidence or changed conditions challenge that actual transfer.

## STR.Preface:13 - Relations - Obtain the professional results the decision needs


FPF is the common conceptual and Method basis. Use the professional practice that can answer the unresolved question on which the strategic choice depends.

Development Opportunity Construction and Development Direction Advising (DOCA) helps find contrasting leads, explain whose problem a proposed contribution addresses, develop a direction or assess whether and how it could be reached. A provisional problem explanation can be a useful result while its support remains incomplete. These Methods can be used directly, with or without an advisory engagement.

Problem Structuring and Decision Support (PSD) can provide a formulation of the decision problem, an account of the participants' values, an uncertainty analysis, a comparison of options or follow-up of an earlier choice. Use the PSD answer as an input when recommending or choosing a direction or commitment.

For a proposed diagnostic service, the following questions illustrate different professional contributions. Obtain only those that can change the strategic decision.

| Question the strategic choice depends on | Professional result to obtain or reuse |
| --- | --- |
| Can the promised service and incident response coexist with current commitments? | An Operations Management (OPS) account of the required service, usable capacity, staffing and response window. |
| Can the organization deliver and accept the whole contribution, including an exception response? | An Organization Change Engineering (OCE) result for the selected arrangement. OCE.9 establishes the contribution and exception path under its permitted conditions, or identifies what remains unavailable. |
| Can the intended practitioner perform meaningfully unfamiliar diagnostic work with the available support? | A Human Capability Development (HCD) result about that person's performance. HCD.12 qualifies transfer from the earlier work to the unfamiliar task; the result retains the actual assistance and conditions. |
| Can the product or platform supply the required technical result? | A Systems Engineering (SYSE) or other qualified engineering result for the relevant configuration, function and acceptance conditions. |
| What does the whole proposal cost and return, and can its payments be met when due? | A qualified financial comparison including provision, support, displaced work, the timing of payments and receipts, and funding conditions. |

For example, missing out-of-hours incident cover in SensorCo's service proposal calls for the service, staffing and cost answers needed to compare the offer. A functioning platform leaves that support question open. STR.8 explains how to locate such a missing contribution; the professional work obtains the answer about the proposed service.

A framework explains how to obtain or qualify a result. The strategic decision needs the applicable professional answer about its actual subject, conditions and horizon, with the limits of the supporting evidence. Check whether an existing answer supplies that contribution; if it does, reuse it. Otherwise ask the responsible practitioner for the missing answer, keeping any dependent commitment conditional.

## STR.Preface:End

# Part I - Locate the Strategic Concern and Uncertainty

<a id="str-1"></a>
## STR.1 - Identify the Strategic Decision, System, and Scope

> **Type:** Method pattern
> **Status:** —

### STR.1:1 - Problem frame

Use this pattern when a request such as “respond to AI”, “find a growth strategy”, or “develop the organization” leaves people working on different decisions. One person is thinking about the next product, another about the company's continuing ability to serve customers, and a third about this quarter's investment approval. The strategy practitioner helps them identify which direction or commitment is actually in question.

Start by asking: **whose contribution could change, which decision can use our answer, and what answer is useful now?** Name the person or organization whose strategy is being considered, the horizon, the affected contribution and the person or body that can make the relevant choice. Distinguish that chooser from the team preparing the answer.

The first useful result is a bounded strategic question that the recipient can use to request a comparison, select an option or clarify a missing condition. A clear question can finish this work. The gain is that later analysis addresses the choice that matters instead of producing an impressive answer to a different one.

Do not reopen the whole strategy frame when an existing frame is adequate and only one assumption has changed; use STR.2 for that impact. If the problem is a late service task within an already selected direction, first return it to the practice responsible for service delivery. It becomes a strategic question when resolving it may change the contribution, direction or commitments being pursued.

### STR.1:2 - Problem

“Strategy” can refer to a desired result, a direction, a plan of work, a business model or a document. Those meanings may all matter, but they are not interchangeable decision subjects. If a request to compare directions is silently treated as approval to build one, preparation becomes an unauthorized commitment. If a question about one service segment becomes a company-wide redesign, relevant differences disappear into an unnecessarily large assignment.

A frame can also be too narrow. A device-pricing question may depend on the field-service contribution those prices used to fund. Treating devices as the entire subject then hides the people and capability whose loss makes the price change strategic.

The difficulty is to choose a boundary wide enough to preserve consequential relations and narrow enough to produce a usable answer in time.

### STR.1:3 - Forces

- A recognizable starting question makes work possible, but an early formulation can conceal the most important alternative.
- The strategic subject needs a usable boundary, while customers, partners and shared capabilities can make the consequences cross it.
- A long horizon exposes durable consequences, but today's chooser may control only a small near-term commitment.
- Clear authority prevents overcommitment, while a team can often complete useful advice before every later permission exists.
- Additional inquiry can clarify a disputed scope, but it consumes time that may be needed for the decision itself.

### STR.1:4 - Solution

Form the smallest strategic question that preserves the contribution, choice and consequences on which the receiving decision depends. Treat the frame as revisable. Use a short conversation or paragraph when that is sufficient; a larger representation is useful only when different participants or later uses need to recover distinctions that a paragraph would lose.

#### STR.1:4.1 - Begin with the consequential change

Ask what has become difficult, newly possible or no longer credible. Connect the concern to a result for somebody: continuing reliable inspection, entering a new customer relationship, sustaining access to a public service or protecting a person's livelihood while developing a new practice.

Separate the observation from its interpretation. “Our inspection price has fallen” can be a supplied fact. “Therefore we should sell an integrated service” is already a proposed response. Preserve the fact while keeping more than one response available.

Identify the kind of concern. An actual loss of the ability to serve a customer differs from a forecast of that loss or an opportunity to serve a different customer. An unresolved choice is not itself proof of a present failure. This distinction determines whether the next answer should address an existing difficulty, a possible future or a newly available contribution.

Then ask what happens if the decision is not made now. A real deadline may arise from a contract, an expiring option or an impending allocation of scarce people. An annual planning date can be useful coordination, but it does not itself prove that every strategic assumption needs revision.

#### STR.1:4.2 - Identify the developing subject and the affected contribution

Name the actual organization, segment, partnership arrangement or person whose direction may change. If participants use the same word but it is unclear whether their accounts concern the same object, establish what each expression refers to, what identifies that object and what would count as its completion or change before treating their accounts as views of one subject. Resolve only the distinction that changes the choice. A product's design can change while the organization remains able to supply its existing service; conversely, an unchanged product may require a different organization capability.

When considering a next-day repair service, the dispatcher may report a customer visit complete once the journey ends, while the customer needs the equipment restored. Before relying on that completion report, distinguish the journey from the repair and use the result the promised service requires.

Distinguish that subject from the means and participants whose development it may need. A more changeable product may still wait months for organizational approval; a trained specialist may still lack access or support. Ask which contribution or working condition limits the proposed direction. The answer can be a small change to how existing work is supported, not replacement of the whole organization.

Inspect one level beyond the proposed boundary when a dependency could reverse the answer. Ask who supplies the capability, who receives the contribution and who bears the consequences. Include the relevant relationship without automatically making every supplier or customer part of the strategic subject.

Where System identity or its boundary is unresolved, FPF A.1.SCR supplies the System-question recovery. An organizational chart, a product name or a strategy document is not enough to settle that identity. When ordinary naming already identifies the subject unambiguously, proceed without a separate ontology exercise.

#### STR.1:4.3 - Distinguish the answer sought now from the later choice

Ask the recipient which result would enable the next useful action. It may be a clarified frame, an account of changed assumptions, a set of feasible directions, a qualified comparison or a recommendation. Request an actual commitment only when it is needed.

Name who prepares the result and who can choose. A strategy team may compare service, licensing and exit while the Board retains the direction decision. The Board may control internal preparation but lack the customer agreement, data permission or financing needed for execution. Keep each limitation at the action it governs; missing trial permission need not prevent a comparison from being completed.

Reuse a sufficient decision-support engagement frame supplied through PSD.1. STR.1 adds the strategic subject, contribution, direction and commitment horizon rather than repeating that engagement method. A distinct adviser relationship may also need DOCA guidance on competence, confidentiality and retained choice.

#### STR.1:4.4 - Fix a useful horizon and boundary

State the horizon over which consequences will be compared and the point by which the next answer is needed. These times can differ. A four-day preparation can serve a twelve-month direction question.

Keep the relevant times in view together: current use, the change being prepared and development of the people or means needed for later changes. They need not occur in sequence. An organization can continue service while improving one enabling condition; the frame should expose the conflict when both require the same people.

Include the current contribution that must continue during transition, relevant resource or exposure limits and serious exclusions. Give a reason for the exclusions. “This question concerns one segment because the remaining product lines have different contracts” is more useful than “out of scope” without explanation.

Do not settle a value conflict by hiding it in the boundary. If two participants disagree about whose service may be reduced, retain that disagreement for the comparison. If two plausible framings imply different beneficiaries or strategic responses, use STR.3. The current frame can state that unresolved distinction without claiming consensus.

#### STR.1:4.5 - Return the bounded question and stop

A usable frame lets the recipient answer five connected questions in ordinary language: whose strategy; which contribution and change; what answer is sought; for which horizon and receiving decision; and who can make the choice or supply a missing condition.

For a consequential engagement, also state the current protected contribution, the exclusion that could otherwise mislead a reader and the observation that would reopen the frame.

If the question cannot yet be bounded, state what prevents it. “We do not know which body can authorize withdrawal from the service contract” identifies the missing answer; “strategy is unclear” leaves the recipient to find the question again. Continue only as far as that missing answer requires. Stop when the recipient can use the bounded question for the intended next step.

### STR.1:5 - Archetypal Grounding

#### STR.1:5.1 - SensorCo: from “respond to AI” to a usable question

SensorCo and all facts in this example are constructed teaching inputs. The company supplies physical inspection sensors and field service. Generic AI-inspection prices have fallen over twelve months; the margin from that offering previously helped fund service. SensorCo also has field-service knowledge and a certified sensor platform.

The initial request is “find our AI strategy for 2027”. The team first distinguishes the inspection product from SensorCo's ability to provide reliable inspection to its customers. A product-feature roadmap would leave the threatened service contribution unexplained.

The resulting question is:

> For SensorCo's affected inspection segment, what can we responsibly pursue and commit to over the next twelve months while sustaining current service? The StrategyTeam prepares the comparison for the Board. It considers device-only continuation, an integrated service, data licensing and segment exit. The Board retains the direction decision and can authorize only the resources and conduct within its established authority.

This frame does not select the integrated service. It names the declining-price premise that STR.2 will examine and the alternatives that later work must compare. Current service and transition duties remain in the question. Data rights and financing are distinct possible conditions, not capabilities conferred by the frame.

The team also distinguishes three possible changes: the inspection offering, SensorCo's way of supplying and accepting service, and the specialists' ability to do that work. The certified platform is an existing means, not evidence that all three changes are feasible. Effective data access or incident cover might be the limiting condition. That possibility belongs in the question without turning the opening frame into a diagnosis or a training commission.

The opening question is now complete enough to begin the needed analysis. The eventual four-day preparation decision belongs to the later comparison and selection; importing it here as a foregone answer would bias the whole exercise.

#### STR.1:5.2 - A professional with eight available hours

A self-directed practitioner asks whether to develop a new paid service. They have eight hours per week after current commitments. An adviser offers a direction, but the practitioner alone can choose how to allocate those hours.

The bounded question is whether to retain the current practice, replace a named activity or undertake a smaller exploration over the next three months without impairing the obligations that protect their livelihood. Six hours of study plus six hours of client development require twelve hours a week, four more than the available eight. That excludes the programme as currently specified while leaving the framed alternatives open.


### STR.1:6 - Bias-Annotation

The person commissioning the work can make their preferred answer appear to be the question: “How do we launch the service?” may conceal a still-open choice about whether to launch. Ask what would make continuation or another direction reasonable before accepting that wording.

Availability bias favours the subject that has a visible document or budget. Check one consequential relationship outside that convenient boundary. Equally, resist making every surrounding relationship part of the engagement merely because it exists.

### STR.1:7 - Conformance Checklist

Use these questions when another participant must rely on the frame.

- Can they identify the strategic subject and contribution, separately from other participants or means that may need development?
- Does the proposed answer address a receiving decision and horizon, with a useful delivery time?
- Are preparation, recommendation and authorized choice distinguishable?
- Is a consequential current obligation or affected party preserved rather than excluded by wording?
- Does any unresolved value, authority or subject question appear as an explicit limitation?
- Can the work end with the bounded frame, and is the next action tied to a named missing result?
- Is the observation that would reopen the frame concrete enough to recognize?

A frame need not answer the later comparison to pass these questions. It must make clear what comparison, if any, is actually needed.

### STR.1:8 - Common Anti-Patterns and How to Avoid Them

**The preferred initiative becomes the problem statement.** A team is asked how to launch a service before anyone has compared that direction. Recover the contribution sought and retain a serious alternative. If the direction has already been selected on a sufficient basis, state that basis and work on the remaining commitment question.

**The document becomes the strategic subject.** Reorganizing a strategy deck can improve communication while leaving the organizational choice unresolved. Name what will change for the organization or its beneficiaries.

**No authority, therefore no useful answer.** A team stops all work because it cannot authorize the eventual investment. Return the comparison or recommendation it can responsibly supply, naming the action that remains blocked.

### STR.1:9 - Consequences

The practitioner can begin with an answer proportionate to the receiving decision. Participants can distinguish a disagreement about scope from a disagreement about alternatives, and later specialists receive a more precise question.

The frame remains an interpretation rather than an assurance of a good strategy. Its cost is a small amount of explicit boundary work and, in disputed cases, the effort to recover an affected participant or authority. Revisit it when a newly discovered relationship changes the available choice, not merely because more detail is available.

### STR.1:10 - Architectural Rationale

A strategic direction connects a desired contribution to capabilities and commitments over time. The subject and receiving decision therefore have to remain visible together: identifying only an organization says too little about the question, while identifying only a decision can hide the contribution it is meant to sustain.

Framing is separate from uncertainty analysis because a clear question may already have sufficient evidence. It is separate from selection because the recipient may need advice without delegating choice. This division allows each result to be used directly and avoids making a whole planning cycle the price of one useful answer.

### STR.1:11 - SoTA-Echoing

**How much framing should precede strategic analysis?** Adopt the receiving-use and choice-owner distinction in the Problem Structuring and Decision Support framework's PSD.1, and adapt it to direction, contribution and commitment over a strategic horizon. A goal-led plan is a serious alternative when the goal, scope and authority are already settled: in that situation it is cheaper to proceed directly. Its defect here is treating a disputed goal or preferred initiative as agreed. Sections 4.1–4.4 therefore recover the question before expanding the analysis, but section 4.5 preserves the direct stop. PSD.1 is reusable practice guidance, not empirical evidence that this particular SensorCo frame will succeed.

**Must goals be fixed before available means are considered?** Rapp, Olbrich and Packard's [2026 analysis of effectuation and judgment](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11846-025-00926-6) is a current conceptual rival to a rigid goal-first account. Adapt its requirement for judgment about means, goals and affordable loss: identify enough of the strategic subject and recipient to make that judgment possible, while allowing the next inquiry to change the goal. The explicit trade-off is a revisable boundary instead of a fully specified plan. The source does not establish a universally superior entrepreneurial method. Reopen this choice if the actual engagement can no longer produce a useful next answer without settling a wider purpose or participant question.

**Why keep several developing subjects in view?** Using a system, creating it and examining how its creators work are different activities. The pattern connects continuous organization development with strategy: a product, an organization and a person's capability can require different changes and different evidence. Sections 4.2–4.4 use that distinction when it changes the frame. A product-only roadmap remains sufficient when surrounding capabilities and conditions are adequately supported; otherwise it can hide the actual constraint. The resulting frame identifies the needed contribution without claiming that one mechanism of learning develops every kind of system.

### STR.1:12 - Relations

STR.2 traces a changed observation to the premise and strategic use it affects. STR.3 compares materially different framings. STR.5 constructs directions once that contribution is needed; STR.11 distinguishes the eventual supported recommendation from authorized commitment.

FPF A.6.P helps recover the concrete objects and claims hidden by shared wording; A.1.SCR helps recover an unresolved System question when that separate question matters. PSD.1 supplies generic engagement and authority-boundary work; DOCA.7 helps govern a distinct development-advising relationship. Reuse their results when they answer the actual question.

### STR.1:End

<a id="str-2"></a>
## STR.2 - Assess How Material Changes Affect Strategic Assumptions and Choices

> **Type:** Method pattern
> **Status:** —

### STR.2:1 - Problem frame

Use this pattern when a price, customer behaviour, capability, constraint, strategic objective or relied-on source has changed and someone asks, “Does this change our strategy?” The strategy practitioner connects the change to the premise and choice it can actually affect.

Begin with the old premise and the changed fact, claim or comparison basis, not a list of all strategic topics. Ask which direction, option or commitment would be different if the premise no longer held. The first useful result is a bounded impact judgment: continue, qualify the premise, reopen the affected choice or return the missing evidence.

The gain is proportionate reconsideration. A material change receives attention where it matters, while unrelated decisions remain usable. A new presentation, publication date or source address does not by itself require a strategy exercise.

If the strategic subject or receiving decision is still unknown, use STR.1. If there is only a routine operational exception with no effect on direction or commitments, return it to the service or operating practice that can resolve it.

### STR.2:2 - Problem

Strategy often relies on premises that are not written as assumptions. A sales plan may assume that buyers will renew at the old price. A service promise may assume that trained staff remain available. A licensing option may depend on a right whose status is unresolved.

Teams can overreact to a visible signal or miss an important one. They redesign everything after a price movement, preserve a preferred direction despite a broken capability premise, or update a source link while leaving the affected comparison unchanged.

A reference list alone cannot show the reach. A receiving decision may use an equivalent premise without citing its source, while a document that mentions the source may not rely on the changed claim at all.

### STR.2:3 - Forces

- Early signals can protect a revisable option, but weak observations can also provoke costly churn.
- Explicit assumptions help recovery, while important strategic reliance often lives in ordinary forecasts and promises.
- Preserving earlier work saves effort, but only where its basis still supports the same use.
- Broad discovery can reveal hidden reliance, while a single known decision may need only one direct comparison.
- A qualified uncertainty statement can be useful even when the decision cannot yet be settled.

### STR.2:4 - Solution

Compare the changed fact, claim or comparison basis with what the strategic decision actually relied on. Follow the consequence only while a receiving action can change. Use sufficient existing evidence before proposing additional inquiry.

#### STR.2:4.1 - State what changed and what remains unknown

Describe the observation with the subject, interval and conditions that change its meaning. “Our three renewal quotes are lower” is not “the market price has permanently collapsed”. “The supplier no longer promises delivery by June” is not evidence that delivery is impossible.

Recover the earlier premise at comparable scope. It may be an explicit model input or an assumption implicit in the chosen direction. Distinguish three kinds of change:

- A change in the world needs the relevant domain evidence: for example, a supplier has withdrawn an available service.
- A changed account needs comparison of the earlier and later claims: for example, a forecast now covers a narrower population.
- A changed basis of choice needs the earlier and proposed or adopted objective, constraint or comparison rule: for example, a new strategic policy admits a kind of commitment previously excluded.

Several can occur together. State what changed in each; proposing a new criterion does not make it applicable, and adopting it does not rewrite earlier observations. Establish who can change a governing condition when its force matters.

If the claims cannot be compared, name the missing fact. An absent old estimate, unknown population or inaccessible contract limits the impact judgment. Uncertainty is a qualified result rather than permission to treat the premise as unchanged.

#### STR.2:4.2 - Find the strategic use

Ask which decision relied on the premise and how. Inspect the actual proposal, commitment or comparison. Would changing this premise alter an option's feasibility, relative merit, scale, timing, permission or required protection?

For one already known use, complete that direct comparison. When a changed source may have several partly unknown uses, use FPF A.10.1 to discover actual reliance within a stated receiving-use boundary. It distinguishes source-based discovery from inspection of receivers that may use the premise without a citation. STR.2 then supplies the strategic judgment for the affected uses; it does not repeat the general source-discovery method.

A practical boundary might be “the two renewal decisions and the service proposal due at this Board meeting”. A no-impact conclusion cannot reach beyond the uses for which its evidence is adequate.

#### STR.2:4.3 - Compare the consequence, not merely the signal

Recover why the premise mattered. A lower generic-inspection price may reduce the attractiveness of expanding that offering without invalidating service already funded by current contracts. Loss of a shared specialist may instead make several proposed directions infeasible at once.

Test the smallest consequence that can settle the use. If the preferred option remains feasible and preferable over the relevant changed range, retain it with the qualified premise. If the changed value crosses a meaningful boundary, reopen the affected comparison or commitment. If the consequence depends on unknown demand or cost, preserve that uncertainty for STR.3 or STR.9 rather than pretending the observation has already selected a response.

If the comparison basis changed, apply the new basis consistently to the affected alternatives. Preserve the old result as an answer under its earlier conditions. A newly important customer use may reopen the option family or problem formulation, not merely adjust a weight in the old ranking.

Use an existing forecast, cost calculation or qualified professional determination when it answers the question. More measurement is worthwhile only when an attainable answer could change the receiving decision before it is needed.

#### STR.2:4.4 - Return one usable disposition

State the effect in the language of the receiving choice. For example: “Do not use the old price in the proposed expansion comparison; current contracted service remains funded under the supplied conditions.” This is more useful than marking the entire strategy red.

When another participant needs to rely on the return, include the observation, the affected premise, the decision and consequence, the evidence limit and the next necessary action.

Keep recommendation and authority separate. Finding that a premise failed can justify advising a pause; it does not grant the analyst permission to cancel an obligation. A service owner may have an established stopping authority, while a Board retains the choice of a new direction. STR.12 connects a later signal to those actions.

#### STR.2:4.5 - Preserve unaffected work and stop

Stop when the bounded receiving question has a supported disposition or a limitation. Follow another dependency only if its result or action could change. A mention of the affected proposal is not enough.

State a useful reopening observation where uncertainty remains: a signed customer term, completed cost component, relevant delivery confirmation or an agreed observation of capacity. The observation needs a receiving decision and useful timing; it is not a request to monitor every available indicator.

### STR.2:5 - Archetypal Grounding

#### STR.2:5.1 - SensorCo: one price change, different consequences

All SensorCo facts are constructed teaching conditions. Generic AI-inspection prices have fallen over twelve months. The StrategyTeam is preparing a twelve-month choice for the affected segment. Existing device and service contracts are assumed to fund the required current service throughout that horizon.

The team inspects three uses of the old price expectation:

| Receiving use | Actual premise | Impact of the supplied change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Proposal to expand the generic-inspection offering | New customers can be served on economics resembling the earlier price level. | Reopen the expansion comparison using the lower-price conditions; the old margin premise no longer supports it as stated. |
| Current service commitment under existing contracts | The identified contracts fund the protected contribution during the horizon. | The new generic-price observation alone does not overturn that supplied funding basis. Preserve the commitment while retaining its actual conditions. |
| Proposal for an integrated service | Customers will pay for accountable inspection outcomes at a cost SensorCo can sustain. | The price decline motivates looking for another contribution but supplies no evidence for this demand or cost premise. Return those as unresolved. |

The result is not “choose integrated service”. It is a bounded correction: generic expansion needs a new comparison, current funded service is preserved and the service option needs its own evidence. The later four-day preparation can address the missing service-cost answer if its burden is justified.

#### STR.2:5.2 - A changed forecast source

Suppose a planning team has used a demand report both in a channel-expansion proposal and in a staffing discussion. A revised report narrows its population to existing customers. The headline estimate is unchanged.

A citation search finds the channel proposal; inspection of the staffing assumptions finds an uncited use of the old population claim. Both uses need comparison at their actual scope. A training note that merely lists the report does not. The source revision affects what the estimate can support, not necessarily the underlying demand.

If the staffing discussion cannot be recovered, the team can finish the channel result while declaring that limit. It cannot claim “no other affected decisions” from the accessible proposal alone.

#### STR.2:5.3 - The observations stay the same, but the filter changes

Consider a constructed strategic filter with four conditions: take changes this quarter that reduce customer rework, can be checked within two weeks and avoid irreversible migration for now. In this example, a reversible correction to error-handling information may satisfy the rule; a proposal requiring irreversible migration is excluded under that last condition. Neither disposition alone awards resources.

The responsible body later adopts a revised policy that permits irreversible migration, subject to specified transition protections. The rework observations and the two-week condition have not changed. The analyst can now reopen the migration proposal's eligibility, but still needs its rework contribution, checkability and transition feasibility. Removing one exclusion does not establish those premises.

The useful return identifies the changed policy premise and the comparison it reopens. The earlier exclusion remains correct under the earlier rule. Current service commitments are not cancelled, and the proposal is not commissioned merely because the new filter permits its consideration. If the policy change were only suggested, the return would remain conditional on its adoption.

### STR.2:6 - Bias-Annotation

A preferred direction encourages selective interpretation: favourable changes become reasons to act, while unfavourable changes become “noise”. State what result would count against the preferred direction before interpreting an ambiguous observation.

Salience also favours spectacular news over quiet loss of a prerequisite. Test the consequence of a missing capability, expiring permission or changed partner commitment even when it has no compelling headline.

### STR.2:7 - Conformance Checklist

For reliance on an impact judgment, check:

- The old premise and changed fact, claim or comparison rule are explicit at the relevant subject and conditions.
- The receiving strategic use actually depends on that premise.
- The consequence states what decision, scale, timing, qualification or protection changes.
- A no-impact conclusion is bounded by the inspected uses and evidence.
- Missing evidence is not counted as unchanged meaning.
- Unaffected work remains usable without being re-proved.
- A proposed response respects the authority needed to act.
- Additional inquiry, if proposed, has an attainable decision-changing result worth its burden.

### STR.2:8 - Common Anti-Patterns and How to Avoid Them

**Headline to pivot.** A new technology announcement is treated as an instruction to abandon the current business. Recover the assumption and compare its consequence before selecting a response.

**Every reference is affected.** The team follows all links from a revised source. Confirm actual reliance in the receiving decision and stop where action cannot change.

**No impact because the number is unchanged.** A report retains its estimate but changes the population, uncertainty or permitted use. Compare the full action-relevant claim.

**No evidence, therefore continue unchanged.** A missing contract or inaccessible estimate is reported as reassurance. Return the scoped uncertainty and let the authorized chooser judge the dependent action.

### STR.2:9 - Consequences

Strategic attention follows actual dependence rather than document activity. A team can correct one comparison, preserve another commitment and leave a third option uncertain without forcing a single status on the whole strategy.

The method costs recovery effort where assumptions were implicit. Its limitation is the coverage and evidence actually available. A narrow, honest result is useful; an unqualified statement about unexamined decisions is not.

### STR.2:10 - Architectural Rationale

New information or a changed comparison basis affects a strategy through its use in a choice or commitment. Making that relation explicit prevents treating news as a decision, dismissing a source revision as mere administration, or silently changing the rule to favour a proposal.

The strategic judgment remains separate from general source-impact discovery. A.10.1 can reveal which uses depend on the changed claim, while Strategy decides what the change means for direction, options and commitments. That separation preserves both reuse and the domain-specific consequence.

### STR.2:11 - SoTA-Echoing

**How should a team respond to changed strategic information?** Adapt the sensing-to-choice relation in Teece's [Dynamic Capabilities: Foundational Concepts (2025)](https://www.cambridge.org/core/elements/dynamic-capabilities/90101DC1EA1A6AFF9228C3FA4CD31930): attention to environmental change should inform the capability and strategic response actually needed. The serious alternative is periodic reconsideration of the whole plan, which can be efficient when many coupled premises change together. For a bounded change, however, that response can spend scarce capacity without altering most decisions. Sections 4.2–4.5 select direct-use comparison and preservation of unaffected work. The source is a theoretical synthesis, not proof that a particular frequency of sensing improves performance; the accepted trade-off is explicit reliance recovery instead of automatic breadth.

**How can a changed source reach an uncited use?** Adopt FPF A.10.1's actual-dependence and bounded-coverage distinction for that branch, rather than treating a citation graph as the impact result. It changes the source example and the no-impact claim in the checklist. A single direct comparison remains cheaper when the one receiving use is already known. Reopen this choice when repeated misses reveal an inadequate discovery boundary or when several strategic consequences can no longer be separated truthfully.

**What if the reported number has not changed?** The changed-premise question includes the population, use, comparison rule and next action. A strategic filter applies that rule to concrete proposals. Strategy revision includes both versioning and filter changes; the pattern distinguishes what must be preserved from what needs reconsideration. Sections 4.1–4.3 and the filter example apply that distinction. Merely replacing values in the old scoring sheet remains sufficient when its basis still fits; it fails when the new use changes eligibility or the meaning of comparison. Preserve prior observations and return only the affected new comparison, not a compulsory restart.

### STR.2:12 - Relations

STR.1 supplies a missing strategic frame. STR.3 qualifies uncertainty or competing interpretations that affect the choice. STR.9 compares alternatives when an old premise changes their relative merit. STR.12 connects material observations to authorized continuation, pause or revision.

FPF A.10 supports claim-bound evidence for one known use. A.10.1 supplies affected-use discovery when a relied-on source changes and the receiving uses are partly unknown; a world-side change without source revision remains a direct strategic question here. Qualified finance, legal or capability results remain with their supplying practices.

### STR.2:End

<a id="str-3"></a>
## STR.3 - Frame Uncertainty and the Strategic Problem

> **Type:** Method pattern
> **Status:** —

### STR.3:1 - Problem frame

Use this pattern when participants disagree about what a strategic change means, or when “we need a new strategy” has not yet become a question that can guide a choice. Start by asking what contribution is at stake, for whom, and how a different account of the difficulty would change the directions worth considering.

The working result is a decision-relevant problem formulation with its material rival formulations and unresolved questions. It connects the situation to strategic direction and possible commitments. A formulation is an account of the situation, not the situation itself. The practitioner can finish this result without choosing a direction, resolving every uncertainty or commissioning a study.

The gain is to put effort into the right question. Falling revenue might call for a pricing response, a different customer contribution, a smaller operating commitment or an orderly withdrawal. Those are not interchangeable interpretations of the same strategic task.

Use an adequate existing formulation directly when no credible rival changes the present action. A known equipment fault with an available qualified repair ordinarily needs that repair, not strategic reframing. More consequential use adds the evidence, participation and professional assurance needed for its factual claims and affected people; a framing conversation supplies none of those results by itself.

### STR.3:2 - Problem

A sponsor's first wording often selects the answer before comparison begins. “How do we become a service company?” excludes continued device provision and exit; “how do we recover device margin?” can exclude a valuable service direction. Both may be useful questions, but neither is neutral.

Another failure combines everything unresolved into “uncertainty”. Unknown demand, disagreement about acceptable losses, missing data-use rights and unavailable engineering time call for different responses. A larger customer survey cannot allocate engineering time or establish permission. Conversely, waiting for complete certainty can prevent a sufficient bounded return.

### STR.3:3 - Forces

The practitioner needs enough openness to notice a different strategic contribution and enough closure to support useful work now. Participants' concerns can reveal a neglected consequence, while agreement among participants does not prove a causal explanation. Existing assets can make a direction attainable but can also bias the discussion toward what the organization already sells.

A longer horizon may reveal opportunities obscured by today's margin. It also introduces less tractable claims. The formulation therefore retains the actual decision window and continuing obligations rather than replacing them with an unconstrained picture of the future.

### STR.3:4 - Solution

Formulate the strategic question so that each material difference changes an information need, feasible direction, consequence or commitment. Keep unlike unresolved matters separate, then return the strongest bounded question and supported claim available.

#### STR.3:4.1 - Recover the difficulty without embedding its remedy

Use STR.1's identified subject, receiving decision and horizon, and STR.2's changed premises when they already answer those questions. Begin from what is observed, anticipated or sought. “Our generic-inspection price fell” is an observation in the supplied case. “Service will restore growth” is a proposed response resting on further claims.

State what makes the situation strategically important: the contribution threatened or sought, the people or organizations affected, and the commitment that may need to change. Separate an actual adverse condition from a possible future difficulty and from an opportunity. All three can warrant strategic work, but they do not supply the same evidence or urgency.

#### STR.3:4.2 - Contrast formulations only where the contrast changes work

Ask which different account could change the beneficiary, objective, included consequences or action family. Keep the strongest plausible rival to the initial formulation; do not create one merely to fill a matrix. A useful contrast might shift attention from protecting a product margin to obtaining a reliable customer outcome with a different business arrangement.

For each retained formulation, explain the action-changing difference in ordinary sentences. What does it foreground? Which evidence would support or weaken it? What action does it make worth considering that the initial wording excluded? A renamed problem with the same consequences adds no useful plurality.

When plural problem construction itself remains difficult, PSD.3, *Generate Plural Problem Formulations*, supplies that contribution. Reuse a sufficient PSD.3 result for the same subject, horizon and receiving decision. This Strategy pattern uses those contrasts to determine which strategic directions and commitments need examination; it does not require repeating the formulation exercise.

#### STR.3:4.3 - Give unlike unresolved matters their own answer

Choose a representation and response that fit the issue. The following distinctions are useful prompts, not a closed taxonomy:

| What remains unresolved | A useful next answer | What that answer can change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A consequence such as demand or delivery cost | A qualified estimate, supported bound or conditional claim | Which directions or commitment sizes remain attractive |
| Competing explanations or future conditions | The assumptions on which their implications differ | Which models, scenarios or option families to retain |
| Whose benefit or loss should govern the choice | An attributed value judgement and the responsible decision | The comparison criterion, not the observed facts |
| A required right or permission | The qualified determination or authorization for the proposed use | Eligibility of dependent action |
| A missing contribution or resource | A feasible way to obtain it, a narrower option or the stated gap | What can actually be undertaken |

An uncertain claim about a right and the absence of the required right are different conditions. Request a determination when the former prevents choice; do not treat the latter as a probability to offset with expected benefit. Likewise, an unknown resource requirement differs from a known requirement exceeding what is available.

PSD.10, *Represent Decision-Relevant Uncertainty and Evidence Limits*, supplies the bounded uncertainty account when a relied-on estimate, model or source limit needs further work. Use its result without converting supported ranges into probability distributions or scenario counts into likelihoods.

#### STR.3:4.4 - Turn uncertainty into a discriminating strategic question

Ask what a different answer could change. It may change the preferred direction, make an option inadmissible, narrow the commitment or show that all current options fail a protected condition. A shared failure matters even if it leaves their ranking unchanged.

A useful question specifies the affected choice and an attainable answer: “At the stated customer price ceiling, can any permitted service configuration cover travel and incident support?” An answer of no can end the current service proposal. “Learn more about customers” gives no such stopping point.

Check whether existing evidence already answers it. When new inquiry would be useful, name the smallest relevant contribution and its time or access limit. STR.7 can judge and design an experiment if an experiment is actually warranted. No claim of eventual solvability makes a costly inquiry worthwhile now.

#### STR.3:4.5 - Return the formulation and the useful next branch

Return the strategic question, material rival formulations, shared and disputed premises, supported claims and unresolved questions. State why each retained contrast changes the next work. Ordinary notes are enough when they preserve this reasoning for the recipient.

Use STR.4 when different future conditions change the choice; STR.5 when a different contribution calls for new directions; or STR.9 when a sufficient option set and comparison basis already exist. If a known constraint excludes the proposed commitment under every retained formulation, return that constraint and any viable narrower action. Reframing need not become a scenario workshop.

Reopen when a changed beneficiary, consequence, objective, resource or credible explanation changes the action families. A new phrase alone does not reopen the question.

### STR.3:5 - Archetypal Grounding

#### STR.3:5.1 - SensorCo: product margin or customer contribution?

In this constructed case, SensorCo's generic AI-inspection price has fallen over twelve months. Existing device and service contracts can still support the required current service for the next twelve months. The team prepares advice; the Board retains the direction and commitment decisions.

The first formulation is “How can SensorCo sustain device provision as generic-inspection prices fall?” It makes device diagnostics, operating costs and continued contracted service salient. The rival is “What reliable inspection contribution could SensorCo supply using its installed base and field-service knowledge?” It opens integrated service and qualified licensing possibilities. Neither formulation establishes that service customers will buy or that licensing rights exist.

The second formulation changes the inquiry. Six interviews establish interest among those respondents, not a conversion rate for the installed base. Travel and incident coverage are missing from the service-cost estimate. Required data-reuse rights for licensing have not been established. The team carries those as three different questions, not one low-confidence service score.

Its useful return is:

> Compare viable device-only continuation with attainable ways to supply a differentiated inspection contribution over twelve months. Protect current service. First determine whether a permitted service arrangement can be economically plausible at the prospective customers' terms; licensing remains conditional on its required right.

Four funded internal days can complete a cost estimate and specify a possible trial. That is a bounded next comparison, not selection of the twelve-month service direction. If sufficient existing cost evidence rules out every relevant service arrangement, the team can return device-only continuation without a trial. If a new class of customer requires a different outcome, the formulation and direction set may need to change rather than merely receive new scores.

#### STR.3:5.2 - Public service: uncertainty or an unresolved value?

A municipal service considers shifting provision between two channels. In this example its responsible body may reallocate a limited budget, but a supplied protected-access obligation remains in force. Demand by channel is uncertain; whose access may be sacrificed is disputed.

The practitioner retains both issues. Existing demand evidence or conditional futures can inform capacity. The responsible value and authority decision governs allowable access consequences. A larger survey cannot decide that obligation's force. If every proposed closure breaches it, the immediate return is the constraint and the search for a feasible configuration, not another demand estimate.

### STR.3:6 - Bias-Annotation

Enterprise cases can privilege revenue, competitive position and management's first concern. Test whether those are actually the receiving subject's purposes. Public access, professional autonomy or continuing customer obligations can change both the frame and the acceptable action.

Plurality can also favour articulate participants. Recover a material affected concern even when its bearer did not formulate a polished strategic alternative; qualify the evidence and attribution rather than treating speaking time as importance.

### STR.3:7 - Conformance Checklist

- The formulation identifies the strategic contribution, subject, receiving choice and horizon.
- Observed difficulty, anticipated condition and desired contribution remain distinguishable.
- Each retained rival changes information, feasible action or consequences.
- Uncertainty, value disagreement, authority and resource conditions receive compatible answers.
- A shared constraint that defeats every option remains visible.
- The return states a supported claim or a discriminating question with its next useful branch and stop.
- Required professional evidence and permissions remain required for their dependent use.

### STR.3:8 - Common Anti-Patterns and How to Avoid Them

**The solution in the question.** “How should we implement service strategy?” turns one proposal into the premise. Recover the contribution sought and retain device continuation when it is a serious rival.

**The infinite uncertainty list.** An inventory of unknowns expands while no decision changes. Name what each consequential answer could permit, reject or narrow; leave unrelated ignorance outside this engagement.

**Consensus as evidence.** A workshop agrees that customers want a new service. Preserve what participants actually reported and distinguish it from demonstrated demand.

**A resource limit treated as research.** The plan needs twelve hours where eight are available. Compare scope or substitution before buying a better forecast.

### STR.3:9 - Consequences

The practitioner can explain why the strategic question changed, what remains contestable and what work would matter next. This reduces effort spent evaluating directions that were never responsive to the actual concern.

A formulation may keep disagreement open. That is useful when its alternatives change action, but it can delay choice. Limit the present return by the real decision window and state what cannot responsibly be settled within it.

### STR.3:10 - Rationale

Strategic framing links a situation to possible contributions and commitments. It therefore precedes neither every observation nor every decision as a compulsory stage. It becomes necessary when an inadequate account would select the wrong evidence, directions or obligations.

Separating the unresolved matters preserves their different remedies. A forecast can improve a consequence estimate; it cannot substitute for a value judgement, permission or supplied capability. The resulting question is usable precisely because it does not promise to settle all of them through one method.

### STR.3:11 - SoTA-Echoing

**How should unresolved uncertainty change a strategic question?** Adapt PSD.3's material formulation contrasts and PSD.10's decision-linked uncertainty to direction and commitment. The serious default is to accept one sponsor formulation and accumulate confidence labels. Sections 4.2–4.4 instead retain only contrasts that change action and identify the answer that could alter choice. This gains a more discriminating question at the cost of examining a credible rival. A sufficient existing formulation is the lower-effort answer and is reused.

For disagreements about future conditions, [Lempert and colleagues' 2024 analysis](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/climate/articles/10.3389/fclim.2024.1380054/full) supplies a substantive robust-decision line: consequential information can matter even when confidence is limited, and several futures can inform action. Adapt that point in section 4.4; reject the need to invent one probability distribution before useful framing. The source concerns climate assessment and decision methods, not empirical validation of this corporate or personal transfer. A defensible probabilistic model remains the serious alternative when it answers the live question.

This pattern distinguishes a changed observation, a changed problem account and a changed comparison rule. Sections 4.1 and 4.5 apply that distinction while retaining alternative perspectives. Reopen the method choice when a supplied remedy closes the question, a new frame changes feasible action, or domain evidence defeats the assumed transfer.

### STR.3:12 - Relations

STR.1 identifies the strategic subject and decision; STR.2 identifies a changed reliance. STR.3 uses those results when they are needed, and returns formulations that can change STR.4's future conditions or STR.5's directions. STR.9 can use an already sufficient formulation directly.

PSD.3 supplies material plural formulation work; PSD.10 supplies qualified decision-linked uncertainty. FPF A.10 qualifies reliance on a particular source claim. Their availability does not establish that their results have already been obtained for this case.

STR.7 considers the worth of an actual proposed experiment. STR.10 examines commitment consequences, including a protected condition shared by otherwise different directions.

### STR.3:End

<a id="str-4"></a>
## STR.4 - Construct Scenarios for Strategic Choices

> **Type:** Method pattern
> **Status:** —

### STR.4:1 - Problem frame

Use this pattern when a strategic choice depends on future conditions that one forecast cannot responsibly settle. Begin with a condition that could change which direction is useful or feasible, then explain a plausible path by which that condition could obtain.

The working result is a small, justified set of future situations for the same strategic question. Each scenario connects assumptions, a causal account and consequences for choice. It helps the practitioner see where a direction works, where it fails and what a materially different future would require.

A scenario describes possible conditions. A forecast makes a predictive claim; a target expresses what someone intends to achieve. Distinguish them before using any of them to support a commitment.

Do not undertake a scenario exercise when a sufficient current comparison or a justified forecast already answers the question. A known constraint can rule out a proposal without any future story. For consequential reliance, obtain the domain evidence and professional judgement needed for the mechanisms and protected limits; an internally coherent story is not evidence that its events will occur.

### STR.4:2 - Problem

Several beautifully named futures can imply the same action. Their narrative variety hides the absence of decision-useful diversity. Another set may be different but combine incompatible assumptions, such as unrestricted customer-data reuse and a restriction that makes that reuse unavailable.

A particularly tempting error turns a preferred future into the baseline and treats the others as deviations. The preferred direction then appears resilient because the scenario set was built around its success. Counting scenarios or assigning equal probabilities does not repair the bias.

### STR.4:3 - Forces

Scenarios need enough structure to explain consequences without pretending to predict a detailed future. A small set is usable but can miss a shared failure; a larger set can consume the attention needed to make a decision.

Familiar developments deserve consideration even when they lack novelty. Unfamiliar conditions can expose hidden dependencies but require a clear basis for treating them as relevant. The practitioner is balancing consequential coverage, explanatory coherence and effort, not maximizing dramatic difference.

### STR.4:4 - Solution

Construct future conditions around the choice they can change. Explain their mechanisms, test their differences and limits, and return the set with the decision questions it exposes.

#### STR.4:4.1 - State the choice and horizon the scenarios must serve

Recover the strategic subject, contribution sought, continuing obligations and decision window. Use STR.3's formulation and unresolved questions if they already exist. Identify what the recipient might choose differently under another condition: a direction, option, scale, timing or protected limit.

Keep the time of commitment distinct from the horizon of consequences. A four-day preparation choice can concern a twelve-month direction; a future event matters to that preparation only if it changes the attainable contribution of those four days.

Reuse an existing scenario set when its assumptions, horizon and consequences fit this use. An attractive industry report about a different population or time window supplies ideas, not automatic coverage.

#### STR.4:4.2 - Choose the conditions with leverage over the decision

Start from uncertain developments and dependencies that can change the comparison. Examples include customer willingness and ability to buy, a necessary permission, rival responses, supply access or a shared service bottleneck. Use source evidence to distinguish an observation, an extrapolation and a deliberately posed stress condition.

Select the smallest productive set. A two-axis matrix can help when two meaningful uncertainties and their combinations account for the differences needed. Use another construction when those axes hide a third condition, create impossible combinations or force irrelevant quadrants. There is no required number or geometry.

Do not confine generation to a fixed list when a new beneficiary, problem or feasible means changes what should be compared. Return that discovery to STR.3 or STR.5. A different direction space is more than a new score on the old scenarios.

#### STR.4:4.3 - Explain how each situation could arise

Write a short causal account: the starting conditions, material changes, their interaction and the resulting situation at the selected horizon. State the assumptions that make the account work. Include only detail that changes interpretation, feasibility, consequences or recognition of the condition.

Then challenge the account. Could the proposed sequence occur within the time available? Do its assumptions fit together? Does it count the same resource twice, rely on an unavailable right or combine incompatible customer behaviours? Retain an uncertain mechanism as uncertain rather than making the prose more confident.

If one uncertain mechanism carries the choice, request its qualified domain answer or retain conditional branches. The scenario's explanatory role does not substitute for that answer.

When another participant's choice can change the comparison, connect each serious own move to that participant's possible responses. State who chooses, what they can observe before choosing, the actions then available, and the supported or hypothetical preferences and constraints. Include the timing and means of any further response of your own. Reuse an adequate current response account; no separate interaction model is needed when such responses cannot change the present choice.

Obtain the qualified game-theoretic or other behavioral result needed for this mechanism. Use a sufficient direct result without building another model account; use PSD.5 when complementary or conflicting model contributions need to be chosen and connected for this question. In a finite sequential model with complete and perfect information, backward induction can resolve later choices before earlier ones. Its relevant common-knowledge and sequential-rationality assumptions must apply: each mover compares outcomes by their own preferences at each possible decision, including contingencies outside the proposed outcome path. Retain materially different tied continuations unless a justified tie-breaking rule resolves them. Return the resulting conditional action profile with its premises, not just a preferred final score.

A declaration alone does not establish the response. If preferences, information, available actions or behavior remain unknown, keep the consequential response branches or request the missing determination. A modelled best response is not an observation or assurance that the participant will behave that way. Simultaneous moves or incomplete information need their appropriate Method, not this sequential calculation by analogy.

#### STR.4:4.4 - Test diversity by its strategic consequences

Compare the conditions against the serious directions or option families. Ask which one becomes preferable, inadmissible, too late or dependent on a different capability. Keep a scenario when that difference matters. Combine redundant stories unless their different mechanisms require different observation or response.

A qualitative account is normally enough: “A full-horizon purchasing freeze removes the opportunity for a paid service trial; a data-use restriction instead changes which service arrangement is permitted.” FPF C.17 supplies the comparison basis and supported-difference discipline if a novelty or diversity claim is needed. It does not generate the scenarios or turn their novelty into likelihood.

Look for a consequential failure common to the options. If every expanding direction depends on the same scarce field-service team, variety in customer futures does not diversify that capacity risk. Examine the shared condition far enough to determine whether it changes scope, generation or the eventual choice.

#### STR.4:4.5 - Return the usable set and its limits

For each scenario, retain the conditions, mechanism, consequential assumptions and implication for the strategic question. Also state what the set leaves outside. A short comparison with explanatory paragraphs can carry this result.
